title: How Does Personalized Memory Shape LLM Behavior? Benchmarking Rational Preference Utilization in Personalized Assistants

bias_targets.methodology: Mechanistic analysis of next-token probability distributions to measure how the presence of irrelevant preference tokens in the context window artificially inflates the probability of conceptually related tokens during response generation.

Generative evaluation using an LLM-as-a-judge and human annotators to assign a severity score (0-5) based on whether the model incorrectly outputs standard, non-personalized content when user preferences should have been applied.

Multi-granularity evaluation involving discriminative intent classification and generative error-pattern analysis to detect when a model inappropriately forces irrelevant user preferences into responses.
